evidence: Cic. Fam. 5.12.4: temporum varietātēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. vicissitūdō)
terms.comment: The general word for things that differ or change: of weather, fortune, colour or food. It also means variety, a range of things (see range).

evidence: Cic. Leg. 2.16: diērum noctiumque vicissitūdinēs (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Eun. 276: omnium rērum, heus, vicissitūdō est
terms.comment: Change that comes round in turn: day and night, the seasons, taking turns in talk (Cic. Off. 1.134).
Rare: Lewis & Short cites only Livy, of a vote taken without any difference among the centuries.

phrases.latin: Jūcundum nīl est, nisi quod reficit varietās.
phrases.english: Nothing is pleasant unless variety freshens it.

sources: Lewis & Short: varietas · Lewis & Short: vicissitudo · Lewis & Short: variatio
